user_input: I want to start a cluster with my software, run some performance tests, and get results. I'd like to use aws. Region and time are not important, cost is...  What should I use?
model_output:
To run a cluster with your software and get performance test results on AWS, you can use the Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) service. EC2 provides scalable computing capacity in the cloud and allows you to run your own virtual machines (called instances) on AWS.

To get started, you can choose an instance type that is appropriate for your workload and desired level of performance. You can also choose a suitable operating system and configure your instance with the appropriate amount of memory, storage, and networking.

Once you have launched your instances, you can use AWS tools such as Amazon CloudWatch, AWS Lambda, or AWS Elastic Load Balancer to monitor and manage your cluster, and to collect and analyze performance data.

It is also important to use a load testing tool to simulate a high number of users accessing your application and measure its performance under stress. Popular load testing tools include Apache JMeter, Gatling, LoadRunner, and NeoLoad.

Finally, you can use cloud cost management tools such as AWS Cost Explorer or AWS Budgets to monitor and control your costs on AWS.
